patterns.name: Accordion
patterns.guidance:
## Accordion

**Also known as:** Arrow toggle  ·  Collapse  ·  Collapsible  ·  Collapsible sections  ·  Details  ·  Disclosure  ·  Expandable  ·  Expander  ·  FAQ block

A vertically stacked set of collapsible sections — each heading toggles between showing a short label and revealing the full content beneath it.

Each heading and its collapsible region form an **Accordion item** — a child of this pattern, not a separate catalog entry.

**Best practices:**
- Use for long-form content that benefits from progressive disclosure
- Keep headings concise and scannable — they are the primary navigation
- Allow multiple sections open simultaneously unless space is critically limited
- Include a subtle expand/collapse icon (chevron) aligned consistently on the right
- Animate open/close with a short ease-out transition (150–250 ms)
- Ensure keyboard navigation: Enter/Space toggles, arrow keys move between headers

**Common layouts:**
- FAQ page with stacked question/answer pairs
- Settings panel with grouped preference sections
- Sidebar filter groups in e-commerce or dashboards
- Mobile navigation with expandable menu sections

---

patterns.name: Alert
patterns.guidance:
## Alert

**Also known as:** Banner (page message)  ·  Callout  ·  Feedback  ·  Inline notification  ·  Message  ·  Notification

A prominent message used to communicate important information or status changes to the user.

For a brief, auto-dismissing, non-blocking message, use a **Toast** (see `toast.md`). Here **Banner** means a page-level message; a top-of-page promotional banner is a **Hero** (see `hero.md`) — and a band named "message banner" or "CTA banner" that carries an image, a headline, and one or two CTAs is that promotional Hero, not an Alert, however the label reads. Alert is the dismissible notification or status message. A continuously scrolling announcement strip is a **Marquee** (see `marquee.md`).

**Best practices:**
- Use semantic color coding: red for errors, amber for warnings, green for success, blue for info
- Include a clear, actionable message — not just a status label
- Provide a dismiss action for non-critical alerts
- Position inline alerts close to the relevant content, not floating arbitrarily
- Use an icon alongside color to ensure accessibility for color-blind users
- Keep alert text to one or two sentences maximum

**Common layouts:**
- Top-of-page banner for system-wide announcements
- Inline form validation message beneath an input field
- Toast notification stack in the bottom-right corner
- Contextual warning inside a card or settings section

---

patterns.name: Avatar
patterns.guidance:
## Avatar

**Also known as:** Portrait  ·  Profile image  ·  Profile photo  ·  User avatar  ·  User image

A visual representation of a user, typically displayed as a photo, illustration, or initials.

An avatar may use a photo as its source, but it is a UI control representing identity — for standalone content imagery, use an **Image** (see `image.md`).

**Best practices:**
- Support three sizes: small (24–32 px), medium (40–48 px), large (64–80 px)
- Fall back gracefully: image → initials → generic icon
- Use a subtle ring or border to separate the avatar from its background
- For groups, stack avatars with a slight overlap and a '+N' overflow indicator
- Ensure the image is loaded lazily with a placeholder shimmer

**Common layouts:**
- User profile header with name and role
- Comment thread with avatar beside each message
- Team member list with stacked avatar group
- Navigation bar user menu trigger

---

patterns.name: Badge
patterns.guidance:
## Badge

**Also known as:** Chip  ·  Label (tag/chip)  ·  Status badge  ·  Status chip  ·  Status pill  ·  Tag  ·  Tag pill

A compact label that sits within or near a larger component to convey status, category, or other metadata.

Here **Label** applies only in a tag/chip sense; a form-field label is the **Label** pattern (see `label.md`). A plain-text category line above a heading is an **Eyebrow** (see `eyebrow.md`), not a Badge.

**Best practices:**
- Keep badge text to one or two words — they are labels, not sentences
- Use a limited palette of badge colors mapped to clear semantics
- Ensure sufficient contrast between badge text and background (WCAG AA minimum)
- Use pill shape (fully rounded corners) for status badges, rounded rectangles for tags
- Avoid overusing badges — if everything is badged, nothing stands out

**Common layouts:**
- Status indicator on a table row (Active, Pending, Archived)
- Tag cloud beneath a blog post or product card
- Notification count on a nav icon
- Feature label on a pricing tier card

---

patterns.name: Breadcrumbs
patterns.guidance:
## Breadcrumbs

**Also known as:** Breadcrumb trail

A trail of links that shows where the current page sits within the site's navigational hierarchy.

**Best practices:**
- Show the full hierarchy path; truncate middle segments on mobile with an ellipsis menu
- The current page should be the last item and should not be a link
- Use a subtle separator (/ or ›) with adequate spacing
- Place breadcrumbs near the top of the content area, below the header
- Keep breadcrumb text lowercase or sentence-case for readability

**Common layouts:**
- E-commerce category → subcategory → product page
- Documentation site section navigation
- Dashboard drill-down from overview to detail view
- File manager path display

---

patterns.name: Button

aliases.name: CTA
aliases.context: triggers an in-page action — submit, open a dialog, toggle; does not navigate

patterns.guidance:
## Button

**Also known as:** CTA (in-page action)

An interactive control that triggers an action — submitting a form, opening a dialog, toggling visibility.

A control that **navigates** (to a URL, page, or anchor) is **not** a Button even when styled like one — it is a **Link** styled as a button (see `link.md`; `<button>` performs an action, `<a href>` navigates). Reserve Button for controls that trigger an in-page action.

For a persistent on/off **state** control, use a **Toggle** (see `toggle.md`), not a Button.

**Best practices:**
- Establish a clear visual hierarchy: primary (filled), secondary (outlined), tertiary (text-only)
- Use verb-first labels: 'Save changes', 'Create project', not 'Okay' or 'Submit'
- Minimum touch target of 44×44 px; desktop buttons at least 36 px tall
- Show a loading spinner inside the button during async actions — disable to prevent double-clicks
- Limit to one primary button per visible viewport section
- Ensure focus ring is visible and high-contrast for keyboard users

**Common layouts:**
- Form footer with primary action right-aligned and secondary action left-aligned
- Hero CTA button centered or left-aligned beneath headline
- Dialog footer with Cancel (secondary) and Confirm (primary)
- Floating action button (FAB) in bottom-right for mobile creation flows

---

patterns.name: Button group
patterns.guidance:
## Button group

**Also known as:** Toolbar

A container that groups related buttons together as a single visual unit.

For a set of mutually exclusive options where only one is selected, use a **Segmented control** (see `segmented-control.md`). A persistent, fixed-position cluster of global page utilities that stays put across scroll — not an in-flow grouping of related buttons — is a **Utility bar** (see `utility-bar.md`).

**Best practices:**
- Group only related actions — unrelated buttons should be separated
- Visually connect buttons with shared border or tight spacing (1–2 px gap)
- Clearly indicate the active/selected state in toggle-style groups
- Keep the group to 2–5 buttons; more options warrant a dropdown or overflow menu
- Wrap the buttons in `role="group"` with an `aria-label`; for toggle-style groups, reflect state with `aria-pressed`

**Common layouts:**
- Text editor toolbar (bold, italic, underline)
- View switcher (grid view, list view)
- Segmented date range selector (Day, Week, Month)
- Split button with primary action and a dropdown for alternatives

---

patterns.name: Card
patterns.guidance:
## Card

**Also known as:** Content tile  ·  Generic card  ·  Tile

A self-contained content block representing a single entity such as a contact, article, or task.

**Best practices:**
- Use a single, clear visual hierarchy within each card: media → title → meta → action
- Keep cards a consistent height in grid layouts — use line clamping for variable text
- When the whole card navigates to one place, anchor the link on the title and stretch it to overlay the card — don't wrap the whole card in one block-level link, which a screen reader reads as a single exhausting link (eyebrow, image, heading, and body run together)
- Keep that link's accessible name equal to the visible title — never a summarizing aria-label that replaces it; raise nested actions (a tag, a Save button) above the overlay so they stay clickable, and use the stretch only when one destination is clearly primary — when several are co-equal, keep discrete links instead
- Use subtle elevation (shadow) or a border — not both simultaneously
- Limit card content to essential info; let the detail page carry the rest

**Common layouts:**
- Product grid with image, title, price, and CTA
- Blog post feed with thumbnail, headline, excerpt, and date
- Dashboard KPI cards with metric, delta, and sparkline
- Team member directory with avatar, name, and role

---

patterns.name: Carousel
patterns.guidance:
## Carousel

**Also known as:** Content slider

A component that cycles through multiple content slides, navigable via swipe, scroll, or button controls.

A strip that scrolls continuously and loops on its own is a **Marquee** (see `marquee.md`) — a Carousel steps through discrete slides, a Marquee moves continuously. Each repeating module inside a Carousel is a **Slide** — a child of this pattern, not a separate catalog entry.

**Best practices:**
- Provide visible navigation arrows and pagination dots
- Support swipe gestures on touch devices
- Auto-advance only if the user hasn't interacted; pause on hover/focus
- Show a peek of the next slide to signal scrollability
- Keep slide count manageable (3–7) — carousels with many slides have low engagement
- Ensure accessibility: each slide should be reachable via keyboard

**Common layouts:**
- Hero image slideshow on a marketing homepage
- Product image gallery on a detail page
- Testimonial carousel with quote, author, and avatar
- Horizontal scrolling feature highlights in a mobile app

---

patterns.name: Checkbox
patterns.guidance:
## Checkbox

A selection control — use in groups for multi-select from a list, or standalone for a single on/off choice.

**Best practices:**
- Use checkboxes for multi-select, not single toggles (use a switch for on/off)
- Align the checkbox to the first line of its label, not the center
- Support indeterminate state for 'select all' when children are partially selected
- Minimum 44 px touch target including label area
- Group related checkboxes under a fieldset with a legend for accessibility

**Common layouts:**
- Filter panel with multi-select facets
- Terms & conditions single checkbox with long label
- To-do list with check/uncheck per item
- Table row multi-select with header 'select all'

---

patterns.name: Color picker
patterns.guidance:
## Color picker

A control that lets users select a color value.

**Best practices:**
- Provide a spectrum picker, hue slider, and direct hex/RGB input
- Include a set of preset swatches for quick selection
- Show a real-time preview of the selected color
- Support copy-paste of hex/RGB/HSL values
- Remember recently used colors for convenience
- Make every control keyboard-operable (arrow keys on the spectrum and hue, number entry for hex/RGB), name it with an `aria-label`, and keep a hex/RGB field as a non-color fallback

**Common layouts:**
- Design tool color picker with spectrum, sliders, and input fields
- Theme customizer with preset palette and custom override
- Annotation tool with color swatch row
- Brand settings with primary/secondary/accent color pickers

---

patterns.name: Combobox
patterns.guidance:
## Combobox

**Also known as:** Autocomplete  ·  Autosuggest

A select-like input enhanced with a free-text field that filters available options as you type.

For a plain value picker without free-text filtering, use a **Select** (see `select.md`).

**Best practices:**
- Show suggestions after 1–2 characters to reduce noise
- Highlight matched text within each suggestion for scannability
- Allow keyboard navigation (arrow keys + Enter) through the dropdown
- Show a 'no results' message instead of an empty dropdown
- Debounce input to avoid excessive API calls (200–300 ms)
- Use `role="combobox"` with `aria-autocomplete="list"`, `aria-expanded`, and `aria-activedescendant` for the active option; announce result counts via a live region

**Common layouts:**
- Search bar with autocomplete suggestions
- Address input with location suggestions
- Tag input that suggests existing tags
- Assignee picker in a project management tool

---

patterns.name: Comparison table
patterns.guidance:
## Comparison table

**Also known as:** Features comparison table

A matrix that compares several entities against a shared set of attributes — entities as columns, attributes as rows, and a boolean or short value in each cell.

For arbitrary tabular data with heterogeneous columns, use a **Table** (see `table.md`); for a single plan's price and CTA, use a **Card** (see `card.md`).

**Best practices:**
- Reach for it when the user's task is "which option includes what" — a fixed attribute set compared across a small number of options, not open-ended data
- Render a real `<table>` with `<th scope="col">` on the entity columns and `<th scope="row">` on the attribute rows, so each cell is announced with its row and column context
- Give every boolean cell a text equivalent ("Included" / "Not included") via visually-hidden text or `aria-label` — never a bare check/cross icon, which is silent to screen readers and ambiguous to colour-blind users
- Optionally emphasize one recommended column, but keep the emphasis to colour/weight plus a text marker, not colour alone
- Collapse gracefully on narrow viewports — a column selector that shows a two-entity subset beats a horizontally scrolling wall of columns
- Keep cell content terse and parallel across a row so the comparison scans vertically

**Common layouts:**
- Product versions or pricing plans as columns, features as rows, check/cross cells
- A highlighted "recommended" or "most popular" column
- Grouped rows with feature-category section headers spanning the row
- Mobile: a column-selector above the table comparing two entities at a time

---

patterns.name: Context menu
patterns.guidance:
## Context menu

**Also known as:** Contextual menu  ·  Long-press menu  ·  Right-click menu

A menu of context-specific actions revealed by right-click (desktop) or long-press (touch) on a target element.

A Context menu is summoned by the user on an object and positioned at the pointer — unlike a **Dropdown menu** (see `dropdown-menu.md`), which hangs off a visible trigger button (including a kebab/overflow icon) and is the better choice when the actions need a discoverable, always-visible affordance.

**Best practices:**
- Always also expose the same actions through a visible control — a right-click-only action is undiscoverable
- Open at the pointer/long-press point; flip to stay within the viewport
- Keep it short; group with separators and put destructive actions last, styled distinctly
- Use the menu ARIA pattern: `role="menu"` / `role="menuitem"`, arrow-key navigation, Enter to activate, Escape to close
- Return focus to the triggering element on close; dismiss on outside click or scroll
- Suppress the native browser menu only where you fully replace it

**Common layouts:**
- Right-click on a table row (Edit, Duplicate, Delete)
- Long-press on a list item or card on mobile
- Canvas/file-browser actions (Rename, Move, Download)
- Text-selection actions in an editor (Cut, Copy, Comment)

---

patterns.name: Date input
patterns.guidance:
## Date input

A date entry control, often split into separate day, month, and year fields.

When users benefit from a visual calendar, use a **Datepicker** (see `datepicker.md`) instead.

**Best practices:**
- Clearly label the expected format (DD/MM/YYYY or MM/DD/YYYY)
- Use separate fields for day, month, and year for unambiguous entry
- Validate in real-time and show errors inline
- Support auto-advancing between fields when a segment is complete
- Label each segment, support Tab and arrow movement between fields, and tie validation errors to the field with `aria-invalid` and `aria-describedby`

**Common layouts:**
- Date of birth entry in a registration form
- Passport/ID expiry date input
- Invoice date field in a financial form

---

patterns.name: Datepicker
patterns.guidance:
## Datepicker

**Also known as:** Calendar  ·  Date Picker  ·  Datetime picker

A calendar-based control for selecting dates visually.

For keyboard-only entry through separate day/month/year fields, use a **Date input** (see `date-input.md`).

**Best practices:**
- Allow both manual text entry and calendar selection
- Clearly indicate the expected date format (e.g., MM/DD/YYYY)
- Highlight today's date and the currently selected date
- Disable dates outside the valid range
- Support keyboard navigation through the calendar grid
- For date ranges, show both start and end in a connected picker
- Render the calendar in a labelled dialog (`role="dialog"`, `aria-modal`), make grid cells arrow-navigable with a visible focus ring, and announce the selected date

**Common layouts:**
- Booking flow with check-in / check-out range picker
- Form field with calendar dropdown on focus
- Dashboard date range filter in a toolbar
- Event creation form with start date and optional end date

---

patterns.name: Drawer
patterns.guidance:
## Drawer

**Also known as:** Flyout  ·  Sheet  ·  Tray

A panel that slides in from a screen edge to reveal secondary content or actions.

A Drawer is non-modal and does **not** trap focus — let focus and Escape return to the page. When the user must finish before continuing, use a **Modal** (see `modal.md`).

**Best practices:**
- Use drawers for secondary content or focused sub-tasks that don't warrant a full page
- Slide in from the right for detail panels, from the left for navigation
- Include a clear close button and support Escape to dismiss
- Dim the background with a semi-transparent overlay to establish focus
- Width should be 320–480 px on desktop; full-width on mobile

**Common layouts:**
- Mobile navigation menu sliding in from the left
- Shopping cart preview panel from the right
- Detail/edit panel in a master-detail layout
- Notification center sliding in from the right

---

patterns.name: Dropdown menu
patterns.guidance:
## Dropdown menu

**Also known as:** Kebab menu  ·  Overflow menu  ·  Select menu

A menu triggered by a button that reveals a list of actions or navigation options — unlike a select, it is not a form input.

Unlike a **Select** (see `select.md`), a Dropdown menu holds no value — use a Select to choose a value, a Dropdown menu to run actions. A menu summoned by right-click or long-press is a **Context menu** (see `context-menu.md`).

**Best practices:**
- Group related items with separators and optional group headings
- Support keyboard navigation: arrow keys to move, Enter to select, Escape to close
- Keep the menu to 7±2 items; use sub-menus or search for longer lists
- Position the menu to avoid viewport overflow — flip to top if near bottom edge
- Indicate destructive actions in red and place them last, separated
- Give the trigger `aria-haspopup="menu"` and `aria-expanded`, use `role="menu"`/`role="menuitem"`, and return focus to the trigger on close

**Common layouts:**
- User account menu in the top-right navigation
- Action menu on a kebab/overflow icon
- Action menu on a table row (Edit, Duplicate, Delete)
- Sort/filter dropdown in a toolbar

---

patterns.name: Empty state
patterns.guidance:
## Empty state

A placeholder shown when a view has no data to display, typically paired with a helpful action or suggestion.

While content is still loading, show a **Skeleton** (see `skeleton.md`) rather than an empty state.

**Best practices:**
- Include a clear illustration or icon to soften the empty feeling
- Write a helpful headline explaining the empty state
- Provide a primary CTA that guides the user toward the next step
- Avoid blame — frame it positively ('No projects yet' not 'You have no projects')
- Show the empty state in-place within the container, not as a full-page takeover

**Common layouts:**
- Empty dashboard with 'Create your first project' CTA
- Search results page with 'No results found' and suggestions
- Empty inbox with illustration and encouraging message
- Empty table with inline prompt to add data

---

patterns.name: Error message
patterns.guidance:
## Error message

**Also known as:** Field error  ·  Inline error  ·  Validation message

Inline validation feedback tied to a single form field, shown when its value is invalid.

An Error message is field-level and bound to a control's validation state — unlike an **Alert** (see `alert.md`), which carries a page- or section-level message. It often occupies the same slot as the field's **Helper text** (see `helper-text.md`), replacing or supplementing it while the error is active.

**Best practices:**
- Be specific and actionable ('Enter a valid email like name@example.com'), not 'Invalid'
- Place it adjacent to the field it describes, directly below the input
- Set `aria-invalid="true"` on the field and link the message with `aria-describedby`
- Announce it with an `aria-live="polite"` (or assertive on submit) region so it is not missed
- Pair color with an icon and text — never signal an error with color alone
- Validate on blur or submit, not on every keystroke; clear the error once corrected

**Common layouts:**
- Single-line error below an invalid text or number field
- Summary of errors at the top of a long form, each linking to its field
- Inline error with a warning icon beside a checkout field
- Password-strength error below a sign-up field

---

patterns.name: Eyebrow
patterns.guidance:
## Eyebrow

**Also known as:** Kicker  ·  Overline

A short text label displayed directly above a heading — categorizing or framing the content it introduces.

The title itself is a **Heading** (see `heading.md`), not an eyebrow; a pill or tag-styled category marker is a **Badge** (see `badge.md`).

**Best practices:**
- Keep it to one to four words — it frames the heading, it is not a sentence
- Style it distinctly from the heading: smaller, letter-spaced or uppercase, in a muted or accent color
- Apply uppercase via CSS `text-transform`, keeping the source text in normal case so it stays legible to screen readers and search
- Mark it up as plain text (`p`/`span`), never a heading element — it must not enter the document outline or compete with the real heading
- Keep the eyebrow out of the section's accessible name — the heading alone names the section, so never chain the eyebrow's id into the heading's `aria-labelledby`
- Ensure the muted eyebrow text still meets WCAG AA contrast; when it is a category link, use a **Link** with a visible focus style

**Common layouts:**
- Category eyebrow above the title on a blog or article card
- Section eyebrow above an h2 in a marketing content band
- Kicker above a hero headline
- Date or topic eyebrow on news-listing items

---

patterns.name: Fieldset
patterns.guidance:
## Fieldset

A container that groups related form fields under a shared label or legend.

A Fieldset groups related inputs within a **Form** (see `form.md`).

**Best practices:**
- Use fieldsets to group related form fields under a descriptive legend
- Style the legend as a section heading within the form
- Ensure the fieldset is announced by screen readers for context

**Common layouts:**
- Address section grouping street, city, state, and zip fields
- Payment information section with card number, expiry, and CVV
- Personal details section in a multi-part form

---

patterns.name: File
patterns.guidance:
## File

**Also known as:** Attachment  ·  Download

A visual representation of a file — such as an uploaded attachment or a downloadable document.

For the control that selects and uploads files, see **File upload** (`file-upload.md`); a File represents the resulting item.

**Best practices:**
- Show file type icon, name, and size clearly
- Include a download action and optionally a preview action
- Display upload date or last modified date
- Use a progress indicator during upload

**Common layouts:**
- Attachment list below a message or form
- File card with icon, name, size, and download button
- Document grid with thumbnails and metadata

---

patterns.name: File upload
patterns.guidance:
## File upload

**Also known as:** Dropzone  ·  File input  ·  File uploader

A control that lets users select and upload files from their device.

Once an upload completes, display each item with the **File** pattern (see `file.md`).

**Best practices:**
- Support drag-and-drop with a clearly defined drop zone
- Show accepted file types and size limits before upload
- Display upload progress with a progress bar per file
- Allow cancellation of in-progress uploads
- Show a preview (thumbnail for images, icon + name for documents) after selection
- Validate file type and size client-side before uploading
- Pair the dropzone with a real `<input type="file">`, keep it keyboard-focusable, and announce upload progress and errors via a live region

**Common layouts:**
- Profile photo upload with circular crop preview
- Document attachment area in a form
- Multi-file drag-and-drop zone with file list below
- Inline file field with browse button and filename display

---

patterns.name: Filter
patterns.guidance:
## Filter

**Also known as:** Facet  ·  Faceted navigation  ·  Facets  ·  Filter panel  ·  Filters  ·  Refinements

A group of controls that narrows a list or search result set by attribute values — each facet exposing its options, typically with result counts.

Entering the query itself is the **Search input** pattern (see `search-input.md`); a Filter refines the result set a search or listing already returned. The value pickers inside a facet are standard form primitives — **Checkbox**, **Radio button**, **Select**, **Combobox**, **Slider** — and applied-filter chips are the **Badge** pattern.

**Best practices:**
- Show a result count next to each value, and hide or disable values that would return zero results
- Pick one application model — filters apply instantly, or apply on an explicit Apply — and use it consistently
- Surface applied filters as removable chips with a "Clear all" affordance
- Group facets into collapsible sections, with the most-used facets expanded by default
- Reflect filter state in the URL so a filtered view is shareable and back-button safe
- Give each facet a `fieldset`/`legend` (or a labeled `role="group"`), announce updated result counts through a live region, and fully manage focus when the filters open in a mobile drawer (the **Drawer** pattern)

**Common layouts:**
- Left-rail facets beside a product grid
- Horizontal filter bar above search results, with applied-filter chips beneath
- Full-screen mobile filter drawer with a sticky Apply button
- Data-table toolbar combining search, column filters, and chips

---

patterns.name: Footer
patterns.guidance:
## Footer

A region at the bottom of a page or section containing copyright info, legal links, or secondary navigation.

Footer links and secondary navigation use the **Navigation** pattern (see `navigation.md`).

**Best practices:**
- Organize links into clear columns by category
- Include essential legal links: Privacy Policy, Terms of Service
- Keep the footer visually distinct but not distracting — muted background
- Include social links and a newsletter signup if appropriate
- Ensure the footer is accessible and links are keyboard-navigable

**Common layouts:**
- Multi-column footer with link groups, logo, and copyright
- Minimal SaaS footer with product links and social icons
- E-commerce footer with help, shipping, returns, and payment icons
- Single-line footer with copyright and key legal links

---

patterns.name: Form
patterns.guidance:
## Form

**Also known as:** Form panel

A collection of input controls that allows users to enter and submit structured data.

Group related inputs with a **Fieldset** (see `fieldset.md`) under a legend; label each control with a **Label** (`label.md`).

**Best practices:**
- Use a single-column layout for most forms — it's faster to scan
- Place labels above inputs for mobile-friendly forms
- Group related fields with visual proximity and optional fieldset headings
- Show inline validation on blur, not on every keystroke
- Disable the submit button until required fields are valid, or show clear errors on submit
- Keep forms as short as possible — ask only what's necessary

**Common layouts:**
- Sign-up form with name, email, password, and CTA
- Multi-step wizard form with progress indicator
- Settings form with grouped preference sections
- Contact form with name, email, subject, and message textarea

---

patterns.name: Header
patterns.guidance:
## Header

The persistent top-of-page region containing the site brand, primary navigation, and key actions.

Primary navigation inside a header is the **Navigation** pattern (see `navigation.md`); for a content title (h1–h6) see **Heading** (`heading.md`), not Header. The page-top title band on an interior page — sometimes called a masthead — is the **Masthead** pattern (see `masthead.md`).

**Best practices:**
- Keep the header height compact (56–72 px) to preserve content space
- Place the logo/brand on the left, primary navigation in the center or right
- Use a sticky header on long pages but consider auto-hide on scroll-down
- Ensure the mobile header collapses into a hamburger menu gracefully
- Maintain clear visual separation from page content (border-bottom or subtle shadow)

**Common layouts:**
- SaaS app header with logo, nav links, search, and user avatar
- Marketing site header with logo, nav links, and CTA button
- Dashboard header with breadcrumbs, page title, and action buttons
- Minimal header with centered logo and hamburger menu

---

patterns.name: Heading
patterns.guidance:
## Heading

A title element that introduces and labels a content section.

For the persistent top-of-page region (brand, nav, actions), see **Header** (`header.md`) — a Heading is a content title (h1–h6), not a page region. A short label line rendered above a heading is an **Eyebrow** (see `eyebrow.md`).

**Best practices:**
- Use a strict heading hierarchy (h1 → h2 → h3) for accessibility and SEO
- Limit to one h1 per page — it's the page title
- Keep headings concise and descriptive — they're the outline of your content
- Use consistent sizing, weight, and spacing across heading levels

**Common layouts:**
- Page title (h1) with section headings (h2) and subsections (h3)
- Card title as an h3 within a page section
- Dashboard section headers separating widget groups

---

patterns.name: Helper text
patterns.guidance:
## Helper text

**Also known as:** Field hint  ·  Hint text  ·  Supporting text

A short, persistent line of guidance shown with a form field to explain its purpose, format, or constraints.

Helper text is neutral guidance that is always visible — it is not the field's name (use a **Label**, see `label.md`) and it is not validation feedback (use an **Error message**, see `error-message.md`, which replaces or supplements helper text when the field is invalid).

**Best practices:**
- Keep it to one short sentence; state the rule positively ('Use 8 or more characters')
- Place it directly below the field (or below the label) so the association is obvious
- Associate it programmatically with `aria-describedby` so screen readers announce it
- Use a muted but accessible color — do not rely on color alone to distinguish it
- Reserve space for it (or for an error in the same slot) to avoid layout shift
- Don't restate the label or duplicate the placeholder

**Common layouts:**
- Format hint below a date or phone field ('MM/DD/YYYY')
- Password requirements below a password field
- Character or word guidance below a textarea
- Privacy reassurance below an email field ('We'll never share this')

---

patterns.name: Hero
patterns.guidance:
## Hero

**Also known as:** Banner (hero area)  ·  Hero banner  ·  Jumbotron  ·  Promo banner

A prominent banner near the top of a page, typically featuring a full-width image or illustration with a headline.

Here **Banner** means the promotional hero area; a page-level message banner is an **Alert** (see `alert.md`). Judge by content, not the label: a promotional band with an image, a headline, and one or two CTAs is a Hero even when a project names it "message banner" or "CTA banner" — the Alert case is the dismissible page notification, not a promotional announcement. The interior-page title band that identifies the page rather than promoting is a **Masthead** (see `masthead.md`); an intro block that opens a content section within a page is a **Section header** (see `section-header.md`).

**Best practices:**
- Lead with a compelling headline — clarity over cleverness
- Limit to one primary CTA and optionally one secondary CTA
- Use a high-quality image or illustration that reinforces the message
- Ensure text contrast against the background image (overlay or safe text zone)
- Keep hero height proportional — it should invite scrolling, not dominate the viewport

**Common layouts:**
- Split hero: headline + CTA on left, product screenshot on right
- Full-bleed background image with centered text overlay
- Minimal hero with large headline, subtext, and inline email capture
- Video background hero with centered headline and play button

---

patterns.name: Icon
patterns.guidance:
## Icon

A small graphic symbol that communicates the purpose or meaning of an interface element at a glance.

For an icon-only control, give it an accessible name — pair the icon with screen-reader-only text (see `visually-hidden.md`) or an `aria-label`.

**Best practices:**
- Use a consistent icon style throughout the product (outlined or filled, not mixed)
- Size icons to align with adjacent text (typically 16–24 px)
- Pair icons with text labels for clarity — icon-only buttons need tooltips
- Use aria-hidden='true' for decorative icons and aria-label for functional ones

**Common layouts:**
- Navigation item with icon + label
- Action button with icon + text ('Download report')
- Status indicator icon beside a label (check, warning, error)
- Icon-only toolbar with tooltips

---

patterns.name: Image
patterns.guidance:
## Image

**Also known as:** Picture

A component for displaying embedded images within a page.

A profile photo shown as an identity control is an **Avatar** (see `avatar.md`); Image is for content imagery such as product shots and featured images.

**Best practices:**
- Always provide meaningful alt text for accessibility
- Use responsive images (srcset) to serve appropriate sizes
- Lazy-load images below the fold for performance
- Reserve space for images before they load to prevent layout shift
- Use modern formats (WebP, AVIF) with fallbacks

**Common layouts:**
- Hero banner with full-width background image
- Product image gallery with thumbnails and zoom
- Blog post featured image above the title or below the headline
- Avatar or profile photo in a circular frame

---

patterns.name: In-page navigation
patterns.guidance:
## In-page navigation

**Also known as:** Jumplinks  ·  On this page

A navigation bar of anchor links that jump to sections within the current page and track which section is in view — the "on this page" contents strip, distinct from site or section navigation.

For navigating between pages or site sections, use **Navigation** (see `navigation.md`); for the accessibility bypass link that skips to main content, use a **Skip link** (see `skip-link.md`); for a single hyperlink, use a **Link** (see `link.md`).

**Best practices:**
- Use when a long page has distinct, headed sections a reader will want to jump between; generate the items from the page's own headings so the two never drift.
- Mark the item for the section currently in view as active, and update it as the reader scrolls (scroll-spy) — do not require a click to change it.
- Render as a landmark: a `<nav>` with an accessible name such as `aria-label="On this page"`, and set `aria-current="true"` on the active item so assistive technology announces position.
- Keep every item keyboard-reachable in reading order (Tab to focus, Enter/Space to activate); moving focus to the target section on activation helps keyboard and screen-reader users.
- Collapse to a compact trigger that shows the active section label on small viewports, expanding to the full list on demand; respect reduced-motion for any scroll or expand animation.
- Anchor targets must be real, focusable headings on the page — never fabricate destinations the content does not have.

**Common layouts:**
- A sticky horizontal pill bar fixed to the bottom or top of the viewport on a long editorial or landing page.
- A left-rail "on this page" list on documentation and long-form article templates, sticky beside the content.
- A collapsed mobile trigger showing the current section, expanding to a drawer of all sections.
- A secondary strip directly beneath a page masthead on a detail page with several stacked content blocks.

---

patterns.name: Label
patterns.guidance:
## Label

**Also known as:** Form label

A text element that identifies and describes a form input.

A status tag/chip sometimes called a label is a **Badge** (see `badge.md`); this pattern covers form-field labels. For guidance text below a field, see **Helper text** (`helper-text.md`) and **Error message** (`error-message.md`).

**Best practices:**
- Always associate labels with their form inputs (htmlFor / id pairing)
- Place labels above the input for vertical forms, beside for horizontal
- Mark required fields clearly (asterisk or 'required' text)
- Keep label text concise — use helper text for additional guidance

**Common layouts:**
- Form field with label above and helper text below
- Inline label beside a toggle or checkbox
- Floating label that moves to the top on input focus

---

patterns.name: Link

aliases.name: CTA
aliases.context: navigates to a URL or page — a call-to-action styled as a button

patterns.guidance:
## Link

**Also known as:** Anchor  ·  Hyperlink  ·  Text link  ·  CTA (navigates)

A clickable reference to another resource — either an external page or a location within the current document.

A **link styled as a button** — a navigating call-to-action — is still a Link. Name it Link; the button styling is a visual treatment, not a change of primitive.

A control that triggers an **in-page action** (submit, open a dialog, toggle) is a **Button**, not a Link (see `button.md`) — a Link navigates, a Button acts.

**Best practices:**
- Make link text descriptive — avoid 'click here' or 'learn more' in isolation
- Underline links in body text for discoverability; nav links may rely on context
- Use a distinct color from surrounding text (but avoid pure blue if it clashes with your palette)
- Show a visited state for content-heavy pages to aid navigation
- External links should indicate they open in a new tab (icon or aria-label)

**Common layouts:**
- Inline text link within a paragraph
- Standalone link beneath a card or section as a 'read more' action
- A heading link stretched to cover a whole card, making the card one click target while keeping its accessible name equal to the visible title
- Footer link columns for site navigation
- Breadcrumb links in a hierarchy path

---

patterns.name: List
patterns.guidance:
## List

**Also known as:** List view

A component that groups related items into an ordered or unordered sequence.

For multi-column data with sortable or filterable columns, use a **Table** (see `table.md`); a List is for flat, single-column sequences.

**Best practices:**
- Use consistent vertical rhythm — equal spacing between list items
- For interactive lists, ensure each row has a clear hover and active state
- Include dividers between items in dense lists; omit them in spacious ones
- Support keyboard navigation when the list is interactive
- Use virtualization (windowing) for lists exceeding ~100 items
- For an interactive list use `role="listbox"`/`role="option"` with `aria-selected` (or `role="list"`/`role="listitem"` when static), arrow-key movement, and a visible focus ring

**Common layouts:**
- Email inbox with sender, subject, preview, and timestamp per row
- Settings list with label, value/toggle, and optional chevron
- Activity feed with avatar, description, and relative timestamp
- File list with icon, name, and size per row

---

patterns.name: Logo bar
patterns.guidance:
## Logo bar

**Also known as:** Logo cloud  ·  Logo wall  ·  Logos bar  ·  Partner logos

A full-width band that presents a row of partner, customer, or certification logos as social proof — often auto-scrolling — with the logos themselves non-interactive.

For a scrolling row of *textual* announcements, use a **Marquee** (see `marquee.md`). For a promotional top-of-page area, use a **Hero** (see `hero.md`).

**Best practices:**
- Use for a trust/social-proof strip of brand logos, not for navigation — the logos are presentational, not links.
- Present the logos as a list of images, each with meaningful `alt` text; mark purely decorative framing `aria-hidden`.
- When the row auto-scrolls, provide an always-visible pause/play control and pause on hover and focus — auto-moving content must be pausable (WCAG 2.2.2 Pause, Stop, Hide).
- Keep the logo track non-focusable and non-interactive; do not attach per-logo click or keyboard behavior.
- Any static aggregate panel (a rating, a customer count) stays separate from the moving track so its content is stable while logos scroll.
- Theme via semantic tokens (light/dark surfaces), never hardcoded brand colors.

**Common layouts:**
- A full-width band directly below the hero as first-screen social proof.
- Static highlight panel beside the logo track on desktop, stacked above it on mobile.
- A partner/customer strip between content sections.
- A trust bar just above the footer.

---

patterns.name: Marquee
patterns.guidance:
## Marquee

**Also known as:** News ticker  ·  Ticker

A strip of content that scrolls continuously and loops automatically — logos, headlines, or announcements moving without user paging.

For discrete slides the user advances one at a time, use a **Carousel** (see `carousel.md`) — a Marquee moves continuously, a Carousel steps. A static, non-moving page-level announcement is an **Alert** (see `alert.md`). A band of brand or partner logos presented as social proof — scrolling or static — is a **Logo bar** (see `logo-bar.md`).

**Best practices:**
- Use only for ambient, supplementary content — never as the sole access path to essential information
- Build the seamless loop by duplicating the content and marking the duplicate `aria-hidden="true"` so it is not announced twice
- Keep the scroll speed slow and steady, and pause on hover and on focus
- Provide a visible pause/stop control — motion that starts automatically and lasts more than five seconds must be pausable (WCAG 2.2.2)
- Honor `prefers-reduced-motion`: render a static or manually scrollable fallback instead of auto-scrolling
- Avoid interactive items in the moving strip; if it must contain links, motion has to pause while any of them holds focus

**Common layouts:**
- Logo-wall marquee of partner or client brands
- News or announcement ticker under the site header
- Stock or score ticker on a dashboard
- Repeating brand-statement band between page sections

---

patterns.name: Masthead
patterns.guidance:
## Masthead

**Also known as:** Article hero

The page-top identity band on interior pages — the page title, often with breadcrumbs and intro text, over an optional background image.

A promotional, CTA-led band that sells is a **Hero** (see `hero.md`) — a Masthead identifies the page, a Hero sells. The persistent site chrome (brand, nav, actions) is the **Header** (see `header.md`), even where publishing vocabulary calls that a masthead. An intro block that opens a section within the page — not the page-top identity band — is a **Section header** (see `section-header.md`).

**Best practices:**
- Contain the page's single h1 here — the masthead carries the page's primary title
- Keep it materially shorter than a homepage hero — a masthead orients, then yields to the content
- Keep breadcrumbs in a consistent position across page templates
- Ensure the title meets WCAG AA contrast over any background media, using a scrim or a reserved safe text zone
- Define focal-point and crop rules for authored background images so the subject survives every breakpoint
- Provide a consistent typographic fallback for the no-media case

**Common layouts:**
- Title and breadcrumbs over a full-width background image
- Text-only band with an eyebrow, h1, and intro paragraph
- Split masthead: title on the left, image on the right
- Compact article masthead with title and metadata (author, date, read time)

---

patterns.name: Media object
patterns.guidance:
## Media object

**Also known as:** Media block

A full-width content band that pairs a block of text — eyebrow, heading, rich text, and a call to action — with a single piece of media (image or video) beside it, the two columns alternating left and right down the page.

For a self-contained entity tile in a grid, use a **Card** (see `card.md`). For the promotional image-and-headline banner at the top of a page, use a **Hero** (see `hero.md`). For a heading-and-intro that opens a section without paired media, use a **Section header** (see `section-header.md`).

**Best practices:**
- Carry one scannable idea per band — a single heading, a short rich-text block, and one primary CTA; a dense grid of items is a Card layout, not this.
- Alternate the media's side between consecutive bands to build vertical rhythm; keep the orientation consistent within a band across breakpoints.
- Stack to a single column on narrow viewports and keep the DOM order media-then-text so the reading order a screen reader announces matches the visual order.
- Wrap the media in a `<figure>`; give a purely decorative image an empty `alt`, and when the media is informative let its `alt` or `<figcaption>` carry the meaning rather than leaning on the adjacent heading.
- Constrain the media to a fixed aspect ratio so successive bands align down the page and the layout does not shift as images load.
- Keep it presentational — a band whose items come from a CMS collection or a recommendation query is a composition of this plus its data source, resolved to its parts.

**Common layouts:**
- A marketing feature band: eyebrow, headline, paragraph, and CTA beside a product image.
- Alternating "how it works" sections down a landing page, the media switching sides each row.
- A full-width video band: a click-to-play video beside supporting copy.
- An image band carrying an overlaid or adjacent pull-quote — a decorative treatment of the same structure.

---

patterns.name: Mega menu
patterns.guidance:
## Mega menu

**Also known as:** Header mega menu  ·  Mega menu panel

A large, full-width disclosure panel opened from a top-level navigation item, presenting a site's sections as several columns of grouped links — often with headings, short descriptions, or a featured tile — with its own open/close, focus, and motion behavior, distinct from the compact bar it drops from.

For the compact site-navigation bar itself, use **Navigation** (see `navigation.md`). For a small single-column menu of actions or links, use a **Dropdown menu** (see `dropdown-menu.md`). For the off-canvas mobile navigation this panel usually collapses into, use a **Drawer** (see `drawer.md`).

**Best practices:**
- Use for a large, grouped navigation surface — multiple columns of links under headings; a small single-column list is a Dropdown menu, not this.
- Open it from a top-level nav item and pair the trigger with `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls` pointing at the panel; the panel takes its accessible name from that trigger.
- Manage focus: move focus into the panel when it opens, keep it within while open, return it to the trigger on close, and close on Escape.
- Treat the contents as a set of links navigable with Tab / Shift-Tab rather than a `menu` / `menuitem` widget, unless you implement the full menu keyboard model.
- On touch and small viewports, collapse into a Drawer or accordion rather than a hover-reveal panel, and never hide a critical task behind hover alone — give a click/tap path and a visible close control.
- Keep each column scannable — a heading plus a short list; push long or promotional content into a single featured tile rather than dense prose.

**Common layouts:**
- A header primary-nav panel: several columns of section links under bold headings, with an optional promoted card or CTA in the last column.
- A products or solutions panel grouping offerings by category with a one-line description each.
- A resources panel mixing link columns with a featured article or media tile.
- A two-tier panel where selecting a left-rail category swaps the right-side link set.

---

patterns.name: Modal
patterns.guidance:
## Modal

**Also known as:** Dialog  ·  Modal window  ·  Popup

An overlay that demands the user's attention — interaction is required before returning to the content beneath.

For a non-blocking panel that slides in from an edge for a secondary task, use a **Drawer** (see `drawer.md`).

**Best practices:**
- Use modals sparingly — only for actions that require immediate attention or focused input
- Always provide a clear close mechanism: X button, Cancel, and Escape key
- Trap focus within the modal while it's open for accessibility
- Return focus to the trigger element when the modal closes
- Keep modal content concise — if it needs scrolling, consider a full page instead
- Use a semi-transparent backdrop to dim the underlying content

**Common layouts:**
- Confirmation dialog with message and two action buttons
- Form modal for quick data entry (create, edit)
- Image/media preview lightbox
- Onboarding or announcement modal with illustration and CTA

---

patterns.name: Navigation
patterns.guidance:
## Navigation

**Also known as:** Hamburger menu  ·  Menu  ·  Nav  ·  Nav bar  ·  Top nav

A region containing links for moving between pages or jumping to sections within the current page.

When navigation lives in a persistent side panel, that panel is a **Sidebar** (see `sidebar.md`); for a bar of links that jump to sections within the current page and track the one in view, use **In-page navigation** (see `in-page-navigation.md`). Use a `<nav>` landmark with an `aria-label` and mark the active item with `aria-current="page"`.

**Best practices:**
- Limit primary navigation to 5–7 items; group the rest under 'More' or sub-menus
- Clearly indicate the current/active page in the navigation
- Use consistent iconography alongside text labels for scannability
- Collapse to a hamburger or bottom tab bar on mobile
- Ensure all navigation items are reachable via keyboard (Tab + Enter)

**Common layouts:**
- Horizontal top nav with logo, links, and user menu
- Vertical sidebar navigation with icon + label and collapsible groups
- Bottom tab bar for mobile apps (Home, Search, Create, Notifications, Profile)
- Mega-menu dropdown with categorized link columns

---

patterns.name: Number input
patterns.guidance:
## Number input

**Also known as:** Number field  ·  Numeric input  ·  Spinbutton

A text field constrained to numeric values, with optional stepper buttons, a min/max range, and a step increment.

A Number input is for typing an arbitrary number (price, age, percentage), with the keyboard as the primary affordance. For nudging a small count up or down with +/− buttons (cart quantity, guests), use a **Stepper** instead (see `stepper.md`); for non-numeric text, use a **Text input** (see `text-input.md`).

**Best practices:**
- Use `inputmode="numeric"` (or `decimal`) so mobile shows the number keypad
- Set `min`, `max`, and `step`; clamp or reject out-of-range values on blur
- Right-align the value when numbers are compared in a column
- Avoid `<input type="number">` for codes, phone numbers, or IDs — use Text input with a pattern instead
- Expose the spinner role to assistive tech: `role="spinbutton"` with `aria-valuenow`, `aria-valuemin`, `aria-valuemax`; support Up/Down arrows and Home/End
- Keep a visible focus ring and label the +/− buttons (`aria-label="Increase"` / `"Decrease"`)

**Common layouts:**
- Quantity field with stepper buttons in a cart line item
- Price or budget input with a currency prefix
- Percentage or weight field in a settings form
- Year or age field in a registration form

---

patterns.name: Pagination
patterns.guidance:
## Pagination

**Also known as:** Page controls  ·  Page nav  ·  Pager

A control for navigating between pages of content when data is split across multiple views.

**Best practices:**
- Show first, last, and a window of pages around the current one
- Use ellipsis to indicate skipped pages, not dozens of page numbers
- Provide Previous/Next buttons in addition to numbered pages
- Clearly style the current page as selected
- Consider infinite scroll or 'Load more' for content feeds

**Common layouts:**
- Table footer with page numbers, rows-per-page selector, and total count
- Search results pagination centered below the results list
- Blog archive with Previous/Next navigation
- API documentation with page controls at top and bottom

---

patterns.name: Popover
patterns.guidance:
## Popover

A floating panel that appears on click near its trigger element — unlike a **Tooltip** (see `tooltip.md`), it can contain interactive content.

**Best practices:**
- Trigger via click, not hover, to support touch devices and accessibility
- Position intelligently to avoid clipping at viewport edges
- Include a subtle arrow/caret pointing to the trigger element
- Dismiss when clicking outside or pressing Escape
- Keep popover content brief — it's not a modal
- Move focus into the popover on open and return it to the trigger on dismiss; it is non-modal, so do not trap focus

**Common layouts:**
- Color picker dropdown triggered by a swatch
- User profile preview card on avatar hover/click
- Quick-edit popover for inline data modification
- Help popover with rich content (text + link)

---

patterns.name: Progress bar
patterns.guidance:
## Progress bar

**Also known as:** Progress

A horizontal indicator showing how far a long-running task has progressed toward completion.

**Best practices:**
- Show a determinate bar when progress is measurable, indeterminate when unknown
- Include a percentage label for accessibility and clarity
- Use color to indicate state: blue/green for normal, red for error, amber for warning
- Animate smoothly — avoid jarring jumps between values
- Keep the bar visually proportional to its container (not too thin to see)

**Common layouts:**
- File upload progress beneath the file name
- Onboarding completion bar in a sidebar or header
- Course progress bar at the top of a lesson page
- System resource usage bar in a monitoring dashboard

---

patterns.name: Progress indicator
patterns.guidance:
## Progress indicator

**Also known as:** Meter  ·  Progress tracker  ·  Stepper (progress)  ·  Steps  ·  Timeline

A visual display of how far a user has advanced through a multi-step process.

Here **Stepper** means a multi-step progress tracker; the numeric +/- input control is the **Stepper** pattern (see `stepper.md`). The multi-step flow that hosts this step display is a **Wizard** (see `wizard.md`). A standalone figure with a describing label — not progress through a sequence — is a **Stat** (see `stat.md`).

**Best practices:**
- Clearly distinguish completed, current, and upcoming steps
- Use numbered or labeled steps — not just dots
- Allow users to click back to completed steps if the flow permits
- Keep the total step count visible so users know the scope
- Vertically stack steps on mobile for readability

**Common layouts:**
- Multi-step checkout (Cart → Shipping → Payment → Confirmation)
- Account setup wizard with profile, preferences, and verification
- Application form with multiple sections
- Project timeline with milestones

---

patterns.name: Quote
patterns.guidance:
## Quote

**Also known as:** Block quote  ·  Pull quote  ·  Testimonial

A styled block for displaying quotations — from a person, an external source, or a highlighted passage.

**Best practices:**
- Use a distinct visual treatment — large quotation marks, left border, or italic text
- Always attribute the quote to its source
- Keep pull quotes short — they're attention-grabbers, not paragraphs

**Common layouts:**
- Testimonial block with photo, quote, name, and title
- Pull quote in a blog post breaking up long text
- Customer quote in a case study with company logo

---

patterns.name: Radio button
patterns.guidance:
## Radio button

**Also known as:** Radio  ·  Radio group

A selection control where the user picks exactly one option from a predefined set.

**Best practices:**
- Use radio buttons for mutually exclusive choices (select one from many)
- Always pre-select a sensible default when possible
- Group under a fieldset with a legend describing the choice
- Stack vertically for more than 2 options — horizontal only for 2–3 short-label options
- Provide sufficient spacing between options (at least 8 px) for easy tapping

**Common layouts:**
- Shipping method selection (Standard, Express, Overnight)
- Payment method chooser with radio + icon + description
- Survey question with single-choice answers
- Plan/tier selection in a pricing form

---

patterns.name: Rating
patterns.guidance:
## Rating

A control that displays or captures a star-based score for a product or item.

**Best practices:**
- Use 5-star scale as the widely understood standard
- Allow half-star precision for display; use full stars for input
- Show the average rating and total review count together
- Use filled/empty stars with sufficient color contrast
- For input, expose a radio group (or `role="slider"`) with arrow-key control and an `aria-label` announcing the current value (for example 3 of 5); for display, provide equivalent text

**Common layouts:**
- Product rating display with stars and review count
- Review submission with interactive star input and text area
- Summary rating card with distribution bar chart

---

patterns.name: Rich text
patterns.guidance:
## Rich text

**Also known as:** Rich text block  ·  Rich text field

A read-only region that renders already-authored formatted content — headings, paragraphs, lists, links, and inline media — as one flowing block styled by the design system, not a surface for composing it.

For an in-page surface where a person *authors* formatted content, use a **Rich text editor** (see `rich-text-editor.md`) — that is the editing tool; this is the render of its output. For a single set-apart quotation, use a **Quote** (see `quote.md`).

**Best practices:**
- Reach for Rich text when a block of authored or CMS-sourced HTML must be displayed as flowing content; style it with element-scoped rules and inter-block rhythm so any well-formed markup renders without per-field classes.
- Render authored headings as real heading elements at the level their position in the page outline requires, and never skip a level — the region itself takes no implicit landmark role and needs no `region`/`aria-label` of its own.
- Keep authored link text as the accessible name; a bare email or phone number is acceptable link text because it is exactly the destination.
- Treat decorative list markers (e.g. checkmark bullets) as `aria-hidden` while the list stays a real `ul`/`li`, so the structure survives for assistive technology.
- Constrain the reading measure for legibility and let embedded media or callouts break out of it, rather than stretching body copy to the full container.
- Scope which blocks may be inserted inline (image, media-with-caption, call-to-action) through an explicit allowlist rather than widening the picker per placement, and treat the authored HTML as untrusted — escape or sanitize before render.

**Common layouts:**
- The body of an article, news post, or policy page.
- A content block dropped into a page-builder column beside other blocks.
- The authored copy inside a card or side panel (a contacts or summary panel).
- A documentation or help region driven from a CMS or markdown source.

---

patterns.name: Rich text editor
patterns.guidance:
## Rich text editor

**Also known as:** RTE  ·  WYSIWYG editor

A WYSIWYG editing surface for creating and formatting rich text content.

For a read-only render of already-authored content, use a **Rich text** (see `rich-text.md`) — this is the editing surface; that is its rendered output.

**Best practices:**
- Provide a minimal default toolbar — reveal advanced formatting on demand
- Support keyboard shortcuts for common formatting (Cmd+B, Cmd+I)
- Ensure pasted content is sanitized to prevent layout-breaking HTML
- Show a word/character count for content with limits

**Common layouts:**
- Blog post editor with formatting toolbar and preview
- Email composer with rich text and attachment support
- Comment editor with basic formatting (bold, italic, link, list)

---

patterns.name: Search input
patterns.guidance:
## Search input

**Also known as:** Search  ·  Search field

A text field designed for entering search queries to find content.

Refining an already-returned result set — by attribute values, with counts — is the **Filter** pattern (see `filter.md`); a Search input enters the query, a Filter narrows the results.

**Best practices:**
- Place a magnifying glass icon inside the field to signal purpose
- Support Cmd/Ctrl+K as a global shortcut to focus the search
- Show recent searches and suggested queries in a dropdown
- Debounce input and show a loading indicator during server queries
- Provide a clear/reset button (×) once text is entered
- Give the field an `aria-label` and `type="search"`; for a suggestions list use the combobox pattern (`aria-expanded`, `aria-controls`) and announce result counts via a live region

**Common layouts:**
- Global search in the top navigation bar
- Command palette overlay (Cmd+K) with categorized results
- Inline search/filter above a data table
- Full-page search with prominent input and categorized results below

---

patterns.name: Search overlay
patterns.guidance:
## Search overlay

**Also known as:** Command palette  ·  Search modal

A full-screen or large surface that opens over the current page to host a search experience — a prominent input with supporting affordances (quick links, recent searches, live suggestions) and its own open/closed and idle/active states.

For a search field that lives inline in the layout, use a **Search input** (see `search-input.md`); for a plain content dialog with no search role, use a **Modal** (see `modal.md`); for inline autosuggest under a field, use a **Combobox** (see `combobox.md`). A Search overlay composes these but adds its own trigger, state machine, and dismissal contract.

**Best practices:**
- Open it from a persistent trigger in global navigation, and give the surface `role="dialog"` with `aria-modal="true"` and an accessible name
- Move focus to the search input on open, trap focus within the overlay, restore focus to the trigger on close, and close on Escape
- Model two states explicitly: an idle state (empty input, quick links / entry points) and an active state (a results panel of recent searches and live suggestions once the user types)
- Expose the suggestions list with combobox semantics (`aria-controls`, `aria-activedescendant`) so arrow keys move through results and Enter selects, without losing the input
- Debounce and announce result updates via a polite live region so screen-reader users hear that suggestions changed
- Dim or inert the page behind the overlay so background content is neither focusable nor read

**Common layouts:**
- Full-screen overlay: centered headline, large input, quick-links grid below
- Top-anchored sheet that slides down from the header, page dimmed beneath
- Idle state with author-managed quick links; active state swapping in a recent-searches + suggestions panel
- A results panel split into "Recent searches" and "Suggestions" columns or stacked sections

---

patterns.name: Section header
patterns.guidance:
## Section header

**Also known as:** Heading with description  ·  Section intro

An intro block that opens a page section — an optional eyebrow above a heading, with a supporting description and optional actions — grouped and aligned as one unit.

This is a section-level intro, not a page masthead: for the top-of-page promotional area use a **Hero** (see `hero.md`); for the site's global top chrome use a **Masthead** (see `masthead.md`). The parts are also catalog primitives on their own — see **Eyebrow** (`eyebrow.md`) and **Heading** (`heading.md`) — the section header is the pattern that composes them.

**Best practices:**
- Reach for a Section header to introduce a content section on an interior page; reach for Hero only when it is the top-of-page promotional band.
- Render the heading as a real heading element at the level its position in the outline requires — a repeating section header owns an `h2`, never the page's single `h1`, which belongs to the hero or page title.
- Treat the eyebrow as a short visual accent (`p`), not a heading — it must not create a phantom level in the document outline or be read as the section's title.
- Collapse each optional part cleanly when unauthored: no reserved space or placeholder for a missing eyebrow or description.
- Apply alignment (start or center) to the eyebrow, heading, and description together as one group, rather than per part, so the block reads as a unit.
- When the description carries inline links or the header carries actions, they follow the Link and Button patterns for focus-visible and keyboard behavior; the header adds no override of its own.

**Common layouts:**
- A left-aligned eyebrow + heading + description opening a content section on a marketing page.
- A centered section intro above a grid of cards or stats ("by the numbers").
- A section header with a trailing "view all" action aligned to the heading row.
- A compact heading + description with no eyebrow, introducing a form or panel.

---

patterns.name: Segmented control
patterns.guidance:
## Segmented control

**Also known as:** Segmented Radio Group  ·  Segmented toggle  ·  Toggle button group

A compact row of mutually exclusive options — a hybrid of button groups, radio buttons, and tabs for switching views.

For grouping independent actions (not a single selection), use a **Button group** (see `button-group.md`); for many options or full content panels, use **Tabs** (see `tabs.md`).

**Best practices:**
- Limit to 2–5 segments — more options warrant tabs or a dropdown
- Use equal-width segments for visual balance
- Animate the selection indicator sliding between options
- Ensure the selected state has strong contrast against unselected
- Use sentence case for segment labels
- Expose it as a `role="radiogroup"` of `role="radio"` segments (or a group of `aria-pressed` buttons); move selection with arrow keys and keep a visible focus ring

**Common layouts:**
- Map/list/grid view switcher
- Billing period toggle (Monthly / Annually)
- Light/dark mode toggle in settings
- Chart type selector (Line, Bar, Pie)

---

patterns.name: Select
patterns.guidance:
## Select

**Also known as:** Dropdown  ·  Select input

A form input that shows the current selection when collapsed and reveals a scrollable option list when expanded.

A button-triggered menu of **actions** is not a Select — that is a **Dropdown menu** (see `dropdown-menu.md`). For a value picker with free-text filtering over many options, use a **Combobox** (see `combobox.md`).

**Best practices:**
- Use native select for simple use cases (better accessibility and mobile UX)
- For custom selects, ensure full keyboard support and ARIA attributes
- Show a placeholder label ('Select an option…') when no value is chosen
- Group long option lists with optgroups or headings
- For searchable selects with many options, use a **Combobox** (see `combobox.md`)
- For a custom select, use `role="combobox"` with `aria-expanded` on the trigger and `role="listbox"`/`role="option"` with `aria-selected` for the popup; support type-ahead and arrow keys

**Common layouts:**
- Country/region picker in an address form
- Sort-by dropdown in a product listing toolbar
- Role selector in a user invitation flow
- Language/locale switcher

---

patterns.name: Separator
patterns.guidance:
## Separator

**Also known as:** Divider  ·  Horizontal rule  ·  Vertical rule

A visual divider — typically a horizontal or vertical line — used to separate content sections.

**Best practices:**
- Use subtle, low-contrast separators — they guide the eye, not dominate it
- Prefer spacing over separators when grouping is already clear
- Use horizontal rules between content sections, vertical rules between columns

**Common layouts:**
- Horizontal divider between list items or content sections
- Vertical separator between sidebar and main content
- Section divider with centered label ('or', 'related content')

---

patterns.name: Sidebar
patterns.guidance:
## Sidebar

**Also known as:** Collapsible sidebar  ·  Side navigation  ·  Sidebar navigation

A persistent vertical panel along the side of the viewport that holds primary navigation and app-level controls.

A Sidebar is the persistent container; the links inside it are the **Navigation** pattern (see `navigation.md`). It differs from a **Drawer** (see `drawer.md`), which slides in over content for a temporary task and is dismissed — a Sidebar stays put (often collapsing to icons rather than disappearing).

**Best practices:**
- Use a `<nav>` landmark with an `aria-label` ('Primary') for the navigation it contains
- Mark the current destination with `aria-current="page"`
- Make it collapsible; persist the collapsed/expanded state and keep labels reachable (tooltip or accessible name when icon-only)
- Below a chosen breakpoint, collapse to a Drawer or hamburger-triggered overlay rather than crushing content
- Keep a visible focus ring and logical Tab order through items and groups
- Don't trap focus — a persistent Sidebar is not modal

**Common layouts:**
- Dashboard/admin shell with icon + label nav and a collapse toggle
- Documentation site with a nested section tree
- Settings layout with section links on the left and content on the right
- Mail/chat app with folders or channels in a collapsible rail

---

patterns.name: Skeleton
patterns.guidance:
## Skeleton

**Also known as:** Skeleton loader

A low-fidelity placeholder that mimics the shape of content while it loads, typically rendered as grey blocks.

When a view has no data at all (rather than loading), show an **Empty state** (see `empty-state.md`) instead.

**Best practices:**
- Match the skeleton shape to the actual content layout as closely as possible
- Use a subtle shimmer/pulse animation to indicate loading — not a spinner
- Avoid skeletons for very fast loads (<300 ms) — they add visual noise
- Show skeleton immediately on navigation; replace atomically when data arrives
- Use muted, low-contrast colors (light gray on white) for skeleton blocks
- Hide skeletons from assistive tech with `aria-hidden` and expose loading via `aria-busy="true"` on the region, so screen readers skip placeholder noise

**Common layouts:**
- Card grid skeleton with image placeholder, title bar, and text lines
- List/feed skeleton with repeating row shapes
- Profile page skeleton with avatar circle and text blocks
- Dashboard skeleton with chart placeholder and metric blocks

---

patterns.name: Skip link
patterns.guidance:
## Skip link

Hidden navigation links that let keyboard users jump directly to the main content, bypassing repeated elements.

It typically lets keyboard users bypass the **Header** (`header.md`) and **Navigation** (`navigation.md`) repeated on every page.

**Best practices:**
- Make it the first focusable element in the DOM
- Visually hidden until focused — then clearly visible
- Link to the main content area with a descriptive label ('Skip to main content')

**Common layouts:**
- Hidden link that appears on Tab focus at the very top of the page

---

patterns.name: Slider
patterns.guidance:
## Slider

**Also known as:** Range field  ·  Range input

A draggable control for selecting a value from within a defined range.

**Best practices:**
- Show the current value in a tooltip or adjacent label
- Use tick marks for discrete value sliders
- Support both dragging and clicking on the track to set value
- Ensure minimum touch target size for the thumb (44 px)
- Pair with a text input for precise value entry when needed
- Expose `role="slider"` with `aria-valuenow`/`aria-valuemin`/`aria-valuemax` (and `aria-valuetext` when units matter); support arrows, Home/End and Page Up/Down with a visible focus ring

**Common layouts:**
- Price range filter with dual thumbs (min/max)
- Volume/brightness control slider
- Image crop zoom level control
- Pricing page seat/usage slider with dynamic price display

---

patterns.name: Spinner
patterns.guidance:
## Spinner

**Also known as:** Loader  ·  Loading

An animated indicator showing that a background process is running and the interface isn't yet interactive.

**Best practices:**
- Show spinners only after a delay (~300 ms) to avoid flicker on fast responses
- Size the spinner proportionally to the context: inline (16 px), button (20 px), page (40+ px)
- Use a single brand-consistent spinner design throughout the app
- Provide an aria-label or sr-only text for screen readers ('Loading…')
- Prefer skeleton screens over spinners when the layout is predictable

**Common layouts:**
- Centered full-page spinner during initial app load
- Inline spinner inside a button during form submission
- Small spinner beside a table cell during lazy-loaded data fetch
- Overlay spinner on a card while its content refreshes

---

patterns.name: Stack
patterns.guidance:
## Stack

A layout utility that applies uniform spacing between its child components.

**Best practices:**
- Use a consistent spacing scale (4, 8, 12, 16, 24, 32, 48 px)
- Default to vertical stacking; support horizontal for inline element groups
- Use stack as a layout primitive to enforce consistent spacing across components

**Common layouts:**
- Vertical stack of form fields with uniform gap
- Horizontal stack of action buttons with gap
- Card content layout with vertical stack of title, description, and meta

---

patterns.name: Stat
patterns.guidance:
## Stat

A compact display of a single quantitative value with a short describing label — a large figure ("98%", "10×", "24/7", "#1") paired with the phrase that gives it meaning, and optionally a supporting sentence or icon.

For a value that tracks progress toward a goal, use a **Progress indicator** (see `progress-indicator.md`); for the card container a stat often sits in, use a **Card** (see `card.md`).

**Best practices:**
- Reach for a Stat when the content is a standalone figure meant to be read at a glance — not a value in a running series and not a measure of progress.
- Keep the value as free-form text; real stats are "98%", "10×", "24/7", "#1", not just integers, so never parse the authored string into a number-plus-suffix or reformat it.
- Pair every value with a short label — the figure alone is not self-describing, and the label carries the meaning for every reader.
- When several stats sit together, equalize them to a shared row or grid and let each grow to its content rather than clipping; a stat that truncates loses its point.
- Give a group of stats an accessible name and expose each pair in reading order value-then-label; when the visible design has no group heading, supply one that is visually hidden and associate the list with it via `aria-labelledby`.
- Treat a decorative figure icon as `aria-hidden` unless it carries meaning the label does not.

**Common layouts:**
- A row of two to four stats beneath a section heading on a marketing page ("by the numbers").
- A single outsized stat as a full-width emphasis band between content sections.
- A stat paired with an icon and a sentence of context inside a card in a feature grid.
- A compact stat strip in a dashboard or report summary header.

---

patterns.name: Stepper
patterns.guidance:
## Stepper

**Also known as:** Counter  ·  Nudger  ·  Quantity

A numeric input with increment and decrement buttons for adjusting a value.

This Stepper is the numeric +/- input control. For a multi-step progress tracker (also called a stepper), see **Progress indicator** (`progress-indicator.md`); for a numeric text field with min/max/step, see **Number input** (`number-input.md`); a multi-step form flow is a **Wizard** (see `wizard.md`), not a Stepper.

**Best practices:**
- Use clear +/- buttons with adequate touch targets
- Allow direct number entry in addition to button interaction
- Set sensible min, max, and step values
- Disable the relevant button when at min or max value
- Expose `role="spinbutton"` with `aria-valuenow`/`aria-valuemin`/`aria-valuemax`, support Up/Down arrows, and label the +/− buttons

**Common layouts:**
- Quantity selector in an e-commerce cart
- Number input for seat count in a booking flow
- Portion size adjuster in a recipe app

---

patterns.name: Table
patterns.guidance:
## Table

A structured grid of rows and columns for displaying data — often called a data table when it supports sorting and filtering.

For a flat, single-column sequence without column operations, use a **List** (see `list.md`).

**Best practices:**
- Use a sticky header row for scrollable tables
- Right-align numeric columns for easy comparison
- Provide sortable column headers with clear sort direction indicators
- Alternate row colors (zebra striping) or use horizontal dividers for readability
- Include a bulk-select checkbox column for actionable tables
- Make tables horizontally scrollable on mobile rather than hiding columns
- Use real `<table>` semantics — `<th>` with `scope`, a `<caption>`, and `aria-sort` on sortable headers — so screen readers can navigate rows and columns

**Common layouts:**
- Admin data table with search, filters, sort, pagination, and row actions
- Pricing comparison table with feature rows and plan columns
- Financial ledger with date, description, amount, and running balance
- Leaderboard table with rank, name, avatar, and score

---

patterns.name: Tabs
patterns.guidance:
## Tabs

**Also known as:** Content tabs  ·  Section tabs  ·  Tabbed interface  ·  Tabset

A set of selectable labels that switch between content panels, keeping the layout compact.

For a compact 2–5 option switch styled as one control, use a **Segmented control** (see `segmented-control.md`).

Each selectable label is a **Tab** and its content region a **Tab panel** — children of this pattern, not separate catalog entries.
